clue.text: Marksman? Formerly a collier

parts.note: ex- is the prefix meaning former or once
a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter who used to work down the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marksman' suggests a rifleman; with the question mark it is someone who awards marks, as in a school exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who awards marks on test papers is the one who sets and grades the tests.

clue.text: Prickly plant Max in hut uprooted

indicators.note: something uprooted is torn up and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Max pulls a spiky weed out of the ground inside his shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprooted' fits a plant, but it tells you to rearrange MAX IN HUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocklebur is a genus of weeds with spiny burrs, a botanical name for a prickly plant.

clue.text: Trader has to rely on financial institution

parts.note: a merchant is a trader
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A dealer must depend on his bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank that deals in corporate finance and acceptances is a type of financial firm.

clue.text: Modern old boat on the Trent!

parts.note: new means modern
the ark is Noah's ancient vessel

explanation.surface: A new version of an ancient vessel is sailing the River Trent.
explanation.walkthrough: The town's full name is Newark-on-Trent, a market town in Nottinghamshire, England; the exclamation mark flags the unusual definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The market town in Nottinghamshire sits beside the river, and its formal name includes the phrase.

clue.text: Telephone round

explanation.definitionFit: To call someone by phone is to give them a buzz, and a circle or hoop is a round shape.

clue.text: Junior is able to become an islander

parts.note: a minor is a junior, someone under age
can means is able to

explanation.surface: A youngster gets the chance to move to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Minorca (Menorca) is one of the Balearic islands of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Balearic isle of Menorca is an inhabitant of that island.

clue.text: Bad turn as it happens

indicators.note: turn tells you to turn the word back to front

parts.note: evil means bad

explanation.surface: Something nasty occurs right in front of you.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast going out in real time, while events unfold, is said to be shown this way.

clue.text: It can be seen to sound similar (or not) at the end

definitions.text: It can be seen to sound similar (or not) at the end

parts.words: It can be seen to sound similar (or not) at the end
parts.note: a poetic device of word endings that look alike on the page though spoken differently, like love and move

explanation.definitionFit: A pairing in poetry where endings are spelt alike, so they match visually, but may not match in pronunciation.

clue.text: Popular individual to stop unknown wickedness

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
I, the single person, is an individual
to quit is to stop
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A well-liked person ending some mystery about sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross injustice or immoral conduct is a synonym for sinfulness.

clue.text: Called back with growl

indicators.note: back says the word for called is read backwards

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Someone phoned back with a snarl.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect or literary word for a snarl or angry grumble.

clue.text: Another outfit needed by driver?

explanation.definitionFit: A fresh set of clothes is a switch of attire, and a motorist shifts from one cog ratio to another.

clue.text: Floral round emblem

parts.note: a globe is a round object
the spiky purple flower is Scotland's national emblem

explanation.surface: A ball-shaped flower that serves as a national symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the plant: its flowerheads are spherical and it is a kind of the Scottish emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Echinops is a plant with spherical spiky blue heads, a round relative of Scotland's national flower.

clue.text: Thief, one old boorish fellow in her embrace

indicators.note: being in her embrace means being held inside the word her

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
jack is an old word for a lout or common fellow

explanation.surface: A robber, an uncouth man of the past, wrapped in a woman's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'in her embrace' wraps the woman's pronoun round the pieces; 'jack' as a lout is an archaic sense, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who seizes a vehicle or goods in transit is a kind of robber.

clue.text: Artist had last letter obliterated

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist
zed is the British name for z, the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A painter had the final character rubbed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A building demolished to the ground has been destroyed completely.

clue.text: Said to be making one suffocate in prison

indicators.note: said to be means the word is heard spoken

parts.note: choky describes something stifling that makes you choke

explanation.surface: Being locked up can feel stifling.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOKEY is British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for jail, from a Hindi word for a lock-up.

clue.text: Stomach's rejecting sooty matter

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: tum is a stomach, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: The belly refuses to accept soot.
explanation.definitionFit: Black particles of soot or grime are a kind of dirt.

clue.text: Reveal plumage in final argument

parts.note: to show is to reveal
down is the fine soft feathering of birds

explanation.surface: A bird displays its feathers in a last dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive confrontation that settles a dispute once and for all.

clue.text: Go to sleep, start nodding at twelve

parts.note: to doze is to nod off

indicators.note: start picks the first letter of nodding

explanation.surface: Nodding off at midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of a dozen-plus-none is a set of twelve; here a collective number word for twelve items.

clue.text: Gradually and progressively from dawn to dark repeatedly

explanation.definitionFit: Step by step over time means gradually, and each sunlit span recurring one after another.

clue.text: Lake one had entered previously

indicators.note: had entered means the one letter has gone inside the word for previously

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone had once gone into a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Noun Enid translated was intimation

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Enid's noun is rendered in another language as a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: An indirect hint or suggestion is a veiled insinuation.

clue.text: Tripe by the yard in Ireland!

parts.note: tripe is a kind of offal
y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Buying tripe in bulk while in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFALY is a county in the Irish midlands; the exclamation mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A county in the midlands of the Republic.

clue.text: Two sets of cards for one on board

parts.note: a deck is a full pack of cards
a hand is the set of cards dealt to one player

explanation.surface: A card game where one player gets two packs.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor working on the vessel's decks is a crew member aboard ship.

clue.text: Tax broken-down car first, it is worn

indicators.note: first puts the rearranged car before the tax
a broken-down car is wrecked, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Before paying tax, the old banger breaks down; this is about car finance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken-down' gives CRA; 'first' says it goes before the tax. 'it is worn' is the definition, a wearable item, not a description of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A neckerchief or wide tie is an item of clothing put on.

clue.text: Very long time ass has been living?

explanation.definitionFit: Ages is the idiom's sense, and a donkey, or ass, lives through its own age span.

clue.text: Some dinner dropped by clumsy person

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of dinner falls on the floor, dropped by an awkward guest.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'by', but 'by' is only the link joining the run to the definition; the definition is 'clumsy person'.
explanation.definitionFit: A socially awkward, inept person is a geek or dork.

clue.text: Calling twice for toy

indicators.note: twice means the call is given two times over

parts.note: yo is a call to get attention

explanation.surface: Shouting twice for a plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool on a string that winds up and down is a classic children's plaything.

clue.text: Initially there is no alternative lady

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A slogan of the Iron Lady, claiming there was no other option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There is no alternative' was Margaret Thatcher's slogan, abbreviated TINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, here a lady.

clue.text: Exhausted after 100 years perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: Worn out by conflict means tired, and a famous Anglo-French conflict lasted a hundred years.

clue.text: Unprepared whilst jumping

explanation.definitionFit: Caught off guard means unready, and hopping is leaping on one foot.
